_comment: Artifact-type registry for the Visual Studio workflow. Downloaded through DownloadTemplate (template_name: datasets/visual_types.json) with an empty template_vars, so this file must contain no doubled-curly-brace placeholder anywhere, not even in a comment. It declares how each type is authored, rendered and formatted; the workflow routes on these fields and adding a type is a data change.
_comment_author: author is one of: image (content -> image prompt -> image model), agent (content -> the pi-render composer authors and renders a composition -> the artifact). The composer plans a storyboard and authors the composition in one turn; the type declares only the output frame (format, aspect, duration, budget).
_comment_render: render is one of: static (a still - a raster the image model authors, or for the composer the final frame of the composition it renders), video (the composer's render, encoded to the type's format), deck (one self-contained HTML presentation authored by the composer, which the same run also renders to video).
_comment_budget: budget.fps/frames/viewport size the composition the composer is briefed to author. A type may declare its own; the workflow passes the type's values to the composer.
_comment_paired: paired declares a second artifact the same run yields: the format of the extra file and the asset type it is returned as. Only a deck declares one.
_comment_duration: durationSeconds is the clip's floor in seconds. secondsPerScene is the minimum each scene gets when the caller names a scene count, so the brief asks for max(durationSeconds, SCENES x secondsPerScene). A type that declares no secondsPerScene keeps its duration whatever the scene count. The GIF type declares none because a per-scene floor would push it past the platform's pixel cap.
_comment_brandKind: brandKind is diagrammatic or photographic. A photographic type is rendered from the brand's photographic art direction with no lettering; a diagrammatic type is rendered from the brand palette in the requested scheme, with lettering.
_comment_default: Requested types come from the caller's ASSET_TYPES parameter (comma-separated). When it is blank, default_types is used. max_types_per_request caps one request.
